titre: The Cadaver Synod, a Pope's Posthumous Trial (897)
accroche: In January 897, a pope has the body of his predecessor, dead for nine months, dug up to be tried seated on a throne.
contenu_vulgarise:
In January 897, in the Lateran Basilica, servants of Pope Stephen VI exhume the body of Formosus, dead nine months earlier, dress it in pontifical vestments and seat it on a throne. A deacon stands beside it to answer in its place. The trial that opens (known in history as the Cadaver Synod) judges a man who can no longer defend himself, for acts dating back years.

## A Verdict That Replays a Power Struggle

The charges against Formosus are not new: he is accused of having held several episcopal sees at once in violation of canon law, of having sworn a false oath, and of having acceded to the papacy while already bishop of Porto, accusations that had already circulated during his lifetime, under the pontificate of John VIII. Stephen VI revives them for a precise political reason: Formosus had crowned Arnulf of Carinthia emperor against the interests of the Spoleto family, to which the new pope is close. The body is declared guilty, his election annulled, all his acts as pontiff erased. Three fingers of his right hand, those used for blessing, are cut off. Stripped of his sacred vestments, dressed in layman's clothes, he is first buried in a common grave, then exhumed a second time and thrown into the Tiber.

## The Trial That Turned Against Its Judge

The spectacle shocks well beyond the circle of Formosus's supporters. A riot breaks out in Rome; Stephen VI is arrested, imprisoned, then strangled in his cell a few months later: less than a year after having had a dead man appear before him. The next pope who has the time, Theodore II, reigns only twenty days, but uses them to annul the synod and have Formosus's body fished out of the Tiber so as to bury it at St. Peter's with honors. John IX, shortly after, confirms the annulment and has the records of the trial destroyed, without preventing chroniclers like Liutprand of Cremona, half a century later, from continuing to tell its details. What the papacy wanted to erase from its own archives ended up surviving in those of its adversaries: the best way to lose control of a story is still to deny it by force rather than answer it.

repere.texte: Formosus is tried nine months after his death; Stephen VI, for his part, dies strangled in prison less than a year after having had him appear.

carte.punch: A pope had the corpse of his predecessor tried, seated on a throne.
carte.idee: In January 897, Pope Stephen VI has the body of his predecessor Formosus, dead nine months earlier, exhumed to be tried dressed as a pontiff on a throne. The verdict declares him guilty, but Stephen VI is strangled in prison the following year, and the synod is annulled.

quiz.question: Why does Stephen VI have Formosus retried, nine months after his death?
choix: Because new evidence of corruption had just been discovered
To erase an imperial coronation that his own political camp contested
Because the canon law of the time required a trial after every pontifical death
To confiscate Formosus's property for the benefit of the Church
quiz.explication: Formosus had crowned Arnulf of Carinthia emperor against the interests of the Spoleto family, close to Stephen VI; the trial replays this political conflict after the fact: no new evidence, no systematic canonical obligation, and confiscation of property is not what motivates the synod.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What verdict and what consequences does the Cadaver Synod pronounce against Formosus?
choix: A dismissal of the case, with immediate return of his pontifical vestments
A simple reprimand, without annulment of his acts
A fine to be paid to the Spoleto family
Guilty, election annulled, all his acts erased, and three fingers of his right hand cut off
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The body is declared guilty, his election annulled and all his acts as pontiff erased; three fingers of his right hand, those used for blessing, are cut off.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does Pope Theodore II do during his short pontificate of twenty days?
choix: He annuls the synod and has Formosus's body fished out of the Tiber to bury it at St. Peter's
He confirms the synod's verdict and has Formosus's archives destroyed
He exiles Formosus's supporters from Rome
He reinstates Stephen VI in his office after his imprisonment
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Theodore II uses his twenty days of pontificate to annul the synod and have Formosus's body fished out of the Tiber so as to bury it at St. Peter's with honors.

quiz_supplementaire.question: How and when does Stephen VI die, after having had Formosus tried?
choix: Of natural causes, two years later, after being deposed
Strangled in prison, less than a year after the trial, following a riot in Rome
Poisoned by a supporter of Formosus at a banquet
Publicly executed on the orders of Emperor Arnulf of Carinthia
quiz_supplementaire.explication: A riot breaks out in Rome after the trial; Stephen VI is arrested, imprisoned, then strangled in his cell a few months later, less than a year after having had a dead man appear before him.
